ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — History and Physical — Babe Didrikson Zaharias — True-date frame: synthetic events are moved into the patient's historical lifetime. Codes, instruments, and treatments remain modern and are anachronistic.

code.originalText: Three months of rectal bleeding, narrower stools and urgency, with tiredness, in a professional golfer of 41: examination, blood tests, and colonoscopy this week

text.paragraph: Three months of rectal bleeding, narrower stools and urgency, with tiredness, in a professional golfer of 41: examination, blood tests, and colonoscopy this week [S]
This fictional modern episode addresses the presenting concerns below. [S]

list.item: Bright red blood with most bowel movements for about three months, stools narrower than before, urgency and a feeling of not having finished; more tired than usual on the course since the end of last season. [S]
A walk-in clinic put the bleeding down to hemorrhoids two months ago and gave her a cream; she is 41, below the age at which screening starts, and was not examined. [S]
She wants to keep competing, and wants to know at once whether whatever this is will mean a colostomy. [S]

text.paragraph: Historical basis. These claims are historical evidence, not findings from a modern examination.

list.item: Mildred Ella Didrikson was born in Port Arthur, Texas, on June 26, 1911, the sixth of seven children of the Norwegian immigrants Ole Nickolene and Hannah Marie (Olson) Didriksen; she later changed the spelling of her surname. In 1915 the family moved to Beaumont, Texas. [D]

Her birth year is given variously: she wrote 1914 on her application for the 1932 Olympics, and some sources, including a historical marker at her grave, give 1913, 1914 or 1915; her gravestone and baptismal certificate support 1911. [D]
At the 1932 Olympic Games in Los Angeles she won gold medals in the javelin and the 80-meter hurdles and a silver medal in the high jump, where her head-first technique was ruled a foul. [D]
She met the professional wrestler George Zaharias at the 1938 Los Angeles Open, and they married on December 23, 1938; he became her manager. [D]

She took up golf in 1933, won 17 amateur tournaments in a row between 1943 and 1947, co-founded the Ladies Professional Golf Association in 1949, and was voted the Associated Press Woman Athlete of the Half-Century in 1950. About 1950 she and her husband bought the Tampa Golf and Country Club in Florida and moved into its converted clubhouse. [D]
By the end of the 1952 golf season she was feeling extremely fatigued. [D]

text.paragraph: 6 later historical claims are omitted because they describe events after the index age. See the teaching note.
Historical biography with true dates. These events are not part of the synthetic care timeline.
No historical medical events are recorded.

list.item: Professional golfer who plays tournaments and exhibitions and practices most days; an Olympic track and field champion in her youth; has never had colorectal cancer screening, which was not yet due at her age [S]
Married, with no children; lives at the golf club she owns in Tampa, Florida, and keeps close ties to her family in Beaumont, Texas. No relative or companion is named or given a role in her care [S]
Never smoker; alcohol rarely; no drug use; eats a varied diet with red meat most days [S]

Periods regular; a levonorgestrel intrauterine device for contraception, placed three years ago; not planning a pregnancy; sexually active, with pain during sex and bleeding afterwards in recent weeks [S]
Fiercely competitive and direct; wants plain facts, and wants to know what any treatment would mean for her game and whether she would need a bag [S]

text.paragraph: No medications started by this date.

Positive for the concerns in the history of present illness. Alert, quick and humorous; worried underneath; PHQ-2 negative; no thoughts of self-harm. No other systems reported as affected in this synthetic episode. [S]

text.paragraph: Alert and engaged. Fully active; plays 18 holes and practices daily, though tired by the back nine for some months (ECOG performance status 0). [S]

Vital signs recorded on 1953-03-16; see the Vital Signs section. Mental status: Alert, quick and humorous; worried underneath; PHQ-2 negative; no thoughts of self-harm. The physical examination is limited to the findings relevant to this synthetic episode. [S]

list.item: Bright red blood with bowel movements for about three months, with narrower stools, urgency, a feeling of incomplete emptying, and a firm, ulcerated mass felt on the back wall of the lower rectum at about 5 cm from the anal verge: a rectal cancer must be confirmed or excluded. Colonoscopy with biopsy booked this week: active, confirmed [S]
Iron deficiency anemia from chronic rectal blood loss: hemoglobin 11.0 g/dL, MCV 77 fL, ferritin 9 ng/mL, with tiredness: active, confirmed [S]

Medical oncology (gastrointestinal) consultation within two weeks, with colorectal surgery, to review the colonoscopy and any biopsy with her and plan staging and treatment if cancer is found. Guideline: NCCN Clinical Practice Guidelines in Oncology: Rectal Cancer (current version); summarized in Benson AB, et al. NCCN Guidelines Insights: Rectal Cancer, Version 3.2024. J Natl Compr Canc Netw 2024;22(6):366-375 (PMID 39151454) (2026); Scott AJ, et al. Management of Locally Advanced Rectal Cancer: ASCO Guideline. J Clin Oncol 2024;42(28):3355-3375 (PMID 39116386) (2024) [S]

Urgent work-up of rectal bleeding with a change in bowel habit and a rectal mass in a woman under 50: colonoscopy with biopsy within days, with mismatch repair testing of any cancer; blood count, ferritin, chemistry and CEA; if cancer is confirmed, rectal-protocol MRI of the pelvis and CT of the chest, abdomen and pelvis; return at once for heavy bleeding, fainting or inability to pass stool. Guideline: NCCN Clinical Practice Guidelines in Oncology: Rectal Cancer (current version); summarized in Benson AB, et al. NCCN Guidelines Insights: Rectal Cancer, Version 3.2024. J Natl Compr Canc Netw 2024;22(6):366-375 (PMID 39151454) (2026); Colorectal Cancer: Screening (JAMA 2021;325(19):1965-1977, PMID 34003218) (2021) [S]

Distress and depression screening at each visit; plain explanations with written information; attention to sexual health and body image and to her golf, with an exercise plan she sets; she decides who is told and who receives each note. Guideline: Ligibel JA, et al. Exercise, Diet, and Weight Management During Cancer Treatment: ASCO Guideline. J Clin Oncol 2022;40(22):2491-2507 (PMID 35576506) (2022); Depression and Suicide Risk in Adults: Screening (2023) [S]
Referral to medical oncology (gastrointestinal), Jun-Ho Albright-Nakamura, MD, ordered 1953-03-16 [S]
